about.size: Common up to about 50 lb; can reach about 100 lb
about.diet: Small fish, crabs and shrimp living in sargassum; also flying fish and mackerels
about.swimming_depth: Epipelagic: surface to about 85 m. Satellite-tagged fish spent about 40% of their time within about 1 m of the surface and made occasional dives to about 250 m.
about.behavior: Offshore, drawn to floating structure (sargassum weedlines, flotsam, floating debris). Moves closer to shore in summer as shelf waters warm.
about.lifespan: About 6 years; fast growing, matures very young

reasons.text: Water is 28.7 C, inside the 25-29 C range where mahi are most active.
Water temperature changes about 0.6 C every 10 km here, one of the sharper breaks in the area today. Mahi gather where warm and cooler water meet.
Chlorophyll is 0.42 mg/m3, in the clean blue-water range mahi favor.
Water color changes rapidly here, marking a chlorophyll front where mahi gather to feed.

factor_diagnostics.value_notes: Satellite tags from 19 wild mahi (2 off Louisiana, 17 off Miami; 2016-2018) recorded 95% of observed time in 25-29 °C SST. The narrower 26.7-27.8 °C association was reported during northward migration, not as a universal South Florida catch optimum. This supports broad thermal occupancy but does not calibrate the configured band as a catch-probability curve.
